basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: A meeting is a convened occurrence with participants, an agenda and a procedure; minutes (WM-REC-012) and decisions (WM-REC-010) are separate records.
It differs from a calendar entry, which only schedules, and from a conferencing platform, which only carries the session.
Its openness is classified before it opens, and closing a portion needs a recorded procedural basis.
It references decisions and tasks without mirroring their state.

may: Compile and circulate an agenda with supporting papers.
Emit a calendar projection of the session.
mustNot: Record, transcribe or analyse a session without a declared purpose and notice to participants.
Close a public session or portion without the required procedure.
Declare a vote result that was not counted under the meeting's rules.
Keep presence or contribution data beyond the procedural or record need.
requiresHuman: Closing a session or portion to the public.
Declaring a vote result with formal effect.
Cancelling or postponing a session with statutory notice requirements.

considerations: Recording and transcription affect participants' privacy and freedom to speak openly.
Open meetings of public bodies serve transparency and accountability.
Remote formats must not exclude participants with disabilities or weak connections.
affectedParties: The public with a right to attend

items: A meeting has a convenor, a time, a place or channel, an agenda and invited participants.
Confused with a calendar event, an informal call, a conference platform session and the minutes.
Invalid decisions due to quorum or notice errors.
Unauthorized recording or sharing of the session.
Leak of content from a closed portion.
RFC 6501 XCON conference information data model.
